extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff and policymakers; USPTO leadership and stakeholders (inventors, patent and trademark practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Fiscal Year 2026 USPTO congressional budget submission providing program goals, performance targets, operational requirements, and quality/timeliness standards for the Patent and Trademark programs and supporting functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Program Goal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Program carries out the USPTO’s mission by optimizing patent quality and timeliness in accordance with laws, regulations, and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program consists of Patent Examining and the PTAB, with support from Patent Information Resources; objectives and initiatives are aligned to deliver strong, reliable, and predictable IP rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve pendency (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve pendency by reducing the size and age of the unexamined patent application inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources support hiring (plans to hire 1,500 patent examiners in FY2026, partially offset by attrition), production incentives, and investments to ensure production output exceeds incoming filings so unexamined UPR inventory declines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue durable patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue durable patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeted investments include prosecution changes, prior art searching, examiner training, and quality initiatives intended to improve patent durability and increase the value of issued patents to inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and address fraudulent and abusive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and address fraudulent and abusive practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding will be used to identify and prevent fraudulent and abusive practices, including targeted staffing and technological tools to detect and combat fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize and streamline examination processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernize and streamline examination processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of artificial intelligence (AI), technological innovations to promote automation, modernization of filing systems (e.g., DOCX), filing assistance, and other IT investments to improve efficiency and CX (customer experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance PTAB policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the policies and procedures of the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources support systematic training, data analytics, policy updates, and procedural changes to improve PTAB decisional quality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-examination (application readiness) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an administrative review to determine whether applications comply with requirements related to form, content, adequacy, and the payment of appropriate fees for paper and electronic filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-examination activities include assigning filing dates, entering bibliographic data into PDP, converting paper filings into electronic images, and supporting pre-grant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining stage: production of office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination stage produces the office actions needed to process patent applications and generates UPR production units to maintain the USPTO’s standards of excellence in patent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A highly educated and specialized workforce (over 9,000 examiners) supported by management, contractors, IT, legal/policy resources, and training is funded to produce estimated production units (e.g., 641,600 UPR production units in FY2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issue processing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Support activities after allowance: prepare patents for issuance, printing, weekly publication, reissues, reexaminations, certificates of correction, processing of application withdrawals, and assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources are required to prepare estimated patents for issuance (e.g., 386,000 patents in FY2026) and to process post-issue matters efficiently to preserve public notice and record integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB AIA trial statutory pendency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA trials must reach a decision on whether to institute trial within three months of the patent owner filing a preliminary response and the PTAB must adjudicate instituted trials within one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB resources are aligned to meet these statutory timelines for institution and final adjudication of AIA trial proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB reexamination appeals timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination appeals must be completed with 'special dispatch'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB allocates resources to ensure reexamination appeals receive expedited handling consistent with statutory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB ex parte appeals inventory management
rubrics_metrics.description: Although ex parte appeals do not have a statutory timeliness requirement, the PTAB remains committed to maintaining strategic pendency and inventory levels, hiring APJs as needed, clearing the oldest cases, and reassigning judges according to greatest need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on strategic pendency, inventory reduction, and enhancing decisional quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB decisional quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB strives to issue reliable and timely decisions by using resources for judicial and legal staff, systematic training, data analytics, and trial-related studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program supports efforts to enhance decisional quality, policies, and procedures and funds PTAB Pro Bono Program support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Information Resources objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance employee experience; improve the patent filing experience; increase patent data quality; increase access to prior art; and provide a highly available and resilient unified case management system for the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives include modernization of USPTO’s patent filing system, new filing capabilities (DOCX), filing assistance, expanded prior art collections, AI technologies, and a unified PTAB case management system to improve both employee and customer experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cutting functions allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-cutting management and support activities (e.g., HR recruiting for patent examiners and APJs, IP policy, financial management) are allocated to the Patent Program based on Activity Based Information (ABI) analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These shared services enable the Patent Program to accomplish goals and are charged appropriately to program budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Reserve policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain two Operating Reserves (patent OR and trademark OR) as a GAO best practice for user fee-funded agencies; deposit a portion of annual fee collections into ORs to align fees and costs over a longer horizon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OR balances finance operations during unexpected economic fluctuations and enable the USPTO to align fees and costs and prepare for demand variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting authority and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee setting authority enables the USPTO to set and adjust fees to align with costs and recover aggregate costs of operations; this authority (per AIA) allows fees to be set via regulatory rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority facilitates investments in strategic goals and responses to legislative requirements; note AIA fee setting authority expiration date (Sept 15, 2026) unless Congress acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency and inventory numeric targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Project year-over-year improvements in unexamined patent inventory (26% reduction by FY2030) and achieve trademark first action pendency goal of 4.5 months by FY2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets are supported by hiring, modernizing processes, and increasing examination capacity; inventory-to-examiner ratios are targeted to reach levels by FY2027 for trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Program Goal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s Trademark Program carries out the USPTO’s mission by optimizing trademark quality and timeliness in accordance with laws, regulations, and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program activities include trademark examining, TTAB, and Trademark Information Resources with objectives to improve pendency, register reliable trademarks, modernize processes, and identify fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve pendency (trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve pendency by reducing the size and age of the unexamined trademark application inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget supports hiring examining attorneys (plans to hire 75 trademark examiners in FY2026, partially offset by attrition), process modernization, and targeted initiatives to reach pendency goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register reliable trademarks / registrability evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining attorneys determine whether a mark is entitled to registration under the Trademark Act by searching previously filed and registered marks to evaluate conflicts and confusing similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners search a database of more than 3 million registered marks and 1.2 million pending marks; approved applications are published for opposition before registration; marks based on intent-to-use proceed to notice of allowance then Statement of Use and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examination quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the quality assurance program, Trademarks reviews the results of an examining attorney’s first and final office actions for the quality of the substantive basis of the decision-making, search strategy, evidence, and writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data from reviews drive electronic and traditional targeted training initiatives; examining attorneys have access to self-paced e-learning and new modules implemented throughout the year based on quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional Office Action standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An Exceptional Office Action reflects correct decision-making, includes excellent evidentiary support, and is exceptionally well written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard expands upon first and final action standards to emphasize comprehensive excellence in final office actions and raise quality expectations cost-effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark maintenance and audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners must file an affidavit attesting use between the fifth and sixth years from registration and renew every 10 years; the USPTO conducts random audits of marks submitted for maintenance or renewal to verify continued use in commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file required affidavits or to substantiate use when audited results in cancellation of the registration to remove unused marks from the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB functions and case handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Trademark Judges on the TTAB review examining attorneys’ adverse registrability determinations (appeals) and conduct opposition and cancellation trial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB adjudicates disputes about registration, conducts hearings, and issues decisions that affect registration outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark electronic input processing and data quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark electronic automated systems transfer tagged application data to appropriate data fields (e.g., classification, design search codes) and are the source of application and registration data available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input processing encompasses Madrid Protocol international applications; investments in information resources support improved data quality and public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and workforce development
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all examining attorneys and patent examiners possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform their jobs via quality programs, targeted training, e-learning, and new training modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is informed by quality review data, supports recruitment and retention, and is considered part of examination costs to improve overall quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource alignment to statutory and workload requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB and examining programs align staffing and resources with projected workloads to meet statutory requirements and program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes hiring APJs and judges as needed, managing inventory, and using data-driven workload models and ABI allocations to plan resource needs.
